title: Personalization in the Era of LLMs - Shivam Verma, Spotify
talk_summary: Spotify's personalization team describes replacing siloed recommender pipelines with a single transformer-based generative recommender: user embeddings, semantic IDs for catalog items, and a projected 'soft token' user representation injected into an LLM prompt. It is a production ML research talk about recommendation quality, not about agent orchestration, cost, or review workflows.

takeaways.technique: Compress bulky state into compact hierarchical tokens
takeaways.what_they_do: They tokenize a ~1000-dim content embedding into 4-6 hierarchical semantic-ID tokens so an LLM can autoregressively predict the next item, instead of pasting raw vectors or IDs into context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it kind of compresses that massive like let's say a thousand dimensional vector into like four or six tokens

takeaways.technique: Single shared representation instead of per-team siloed models
takeaways.what_they_do: They are consolidating many product-specific recommender models into one unified backbone with a shared user representation, so downstream surfaces reuse the same foundation.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're kind of moving away from that sort of siloed model of working towards this single unified model
